I went through the `/code-conventions` checklist in `--review-pr` mode and considered all 57 rules against `f6f337674...HEAD`. The diff touches two files, `src/modules/auth/utils/auth-redirect.helper.ts` and `src/modules/auth/utils/auth-redirect.helper.spec.ts`. The checklist was written to the scratchpad, so no tracked files changed, and I ran no tests.

**Rules that applied:** SEC-01, CONFIG-01, CONFIG-05, PR-02, STYLE-01, NAME-01, TEST-01, TEST-02, TEST-04, TEST-08, TEST-09, CHANGE-01, and the SPDX license-header rule. The other rules (MOD, DB, CACHE, ROUTE, TYPE, PERF, LOG, RESILIENCE and so on) don't apply to this diff. I didn't need to look up the review history behind any rule.

**Passes:** Both files have the SPDX header. The helper is still a small private function with up-to-date JSDoc. The tests are unit tests at the right level (TEST-02) and use faker. The rejection cases are well covered (TEST-04): lookalike hostnames, userinfo, non-HTTP schemes, and production. Hostnames are matched exactly with a `Set`, and URL parsing folds `127.1` and `0x7f000001` into `127.0.0.1`, so there's no suffix or prefix bypass.

## Findings

**1. The `AUTH_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_DOMAIN` description is now out of date (PR-02, CONFIG-05). Medium.**
`.env.sample.json:118` still says setting the variable means "any subdomain is accepted". After this PR, setting it also allows `http`/`https` redirects to `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]` on any port (`src/modules/auth/utils/auth-redirect.helper.ts:139-141`). An operator reading the sample won't know that turning on subdomain redirects also turns on loopback redirects. **Fix:** update the description in this PR.

**2. The new tests can fail at random because of URL port normalisation (TEST-09). Low.**
`src/modules/auth/utils/auth-redirect.helper.spec.ts:212` builds `http://${host}:${faker.internet.port()}/...` and expects `toBe(url)`. Line 224 does the same for `https://localhost:${port}`. If faker picks 80 (http) or 443 (https), `new URL(...).toString()` drops the default port, and the check fails. I confirmed this with Node: `http://localhost:80/x` becomes `http://localhost/x`. It's rare (about 1 in 65k per test), but it will happen eventually. **Fix:** use a fixed non-default port, or pick one from a range that excludes 80 and 443.

**3. Test placement and naming (TEST-08). Low.**
- `auth-redirect.helper.spec.ts:254`: `should reject loopback in production` sits inside `describe('non-production with allowedRedirectDomain')` (line 151) and builds its own production config. Move it to the `production (same-origin check)` block (line 97), or put the loopback tests in their own `describe`.
- `auth-redirect.helper.spec.ts:233`: `lookalike hostname suffixed with allowed name` tests `localhost.<random-domain>`. That's a loopback name with a domain added after it, and nothing to do with `allowedRedirectDomain`. A clearer name would be "loopback name followed by an extra domain label".
- Minor: the userinfo and `ftp` cases (lines 242 and 246) hard-code port `3000`, while the other cases use faker.

**4. The loopback exception has no separate switch (SEC-01, CONFIG-01). Advisory, for reviewers to decide.**
SEC-01 requires strict checks on protocol and port, and CONFIG-01 wants conservative defaults. This PR relaxes both for loopback in every non-production environment that sets `AUTH_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_DOMAIN` (`auth-redirect.helper.ts:130-141`). Those environments include staging, not only `CGW_ENV === 'development'`. The JSDoc cites RFC 8252 §7.3, which covers native apps; here it's being applied to browser redirects on deployed environments.
- Impact looks low. The OIDC state only stores the URL (`src/modules/auth/oidc/routes/oidc-auth.service.ts:128-135`), and the logout `returnTo` goes through Auth0's own allowed-logout-URL list (`src/modules/auth/routes/auth.service.ts:147`).
- Still, it's a security relaxation turned on by an unrelated setting. Reviewers should either accept it explicitly or put it behind its own flag. Also note that Auth0's allowed callback/logout URLs must include the loopback origins for logout to work.

**5. Missing blank line (STYLE-01). Nit.**
At `src/modules/auth/utils/auth-redirect.helper.ts:6-7`, the new `LOOPBACK_HOSTNAMES` constant runs straight into the JSDoc of `buildAuth0LogoutBaseUrl` with no blank line in between. The earlier `AUTH0_LOGOUT_PATH` line already lacked one, and the new constant continues that.

**Still open:** finding 1 should be fixed before merge. Finding 4 needs an explicit call from the team. Findings 2, 3 and 5 are small test and style fixes.
